title: Lamentations 1: chapter overview
paragraphs: The miserable state of Jerusalem, the just consequences of its sins. (Lam. 1:1-11) Jerusalem represented as a captive female, lamenting, and seeking the mercy of God. (Lam. 1:12-22)
Lam. 1:1-11 The prophet sometimes speaks in his own person; at other times Jerusalem, as a distressed female, is the speaker, or some of the Jews.

context: It is evident that Jeremiah was the author of the Lamentations which bear his name.
attribution: Matthew Henry, Concise Commentary (public domain). Historical Protestant interpretation; other traditions may read these passages differently.

title: Lamentations 2: chapter overview
paragraphs: Lamentation for the misery of Jerusalem.
Lam. 2:1-9 A sad representation is here made of the state of God's church, of Jacob and Israel; but the notice seems mostly to refer to the hand of the Lord in their calamities.

title: Lamentations 3: chapter overview
paragraphs: The faithful lament their calamities, and hope in God's mercies.
Lam. 3:1-20 The prophet relates the more gloomy and discouraging part of his experience, and how he found support and relief.

title: Lamentations 4: chapter overview
paragraphs: The deplorable state of the nation is contrasted with its ancient prosperity.
Lam. 4:1-12 What a change is here!
